summary: Discovery call focused on security and compliance requirements for Catalyst Health evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Main concerns: SOC2/ISO attestation, SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC granularity, audit log retention and export, encryption at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), data residency in US/EU, and retention/purge policies. Catalyst prefers Private for PHI-sensitive workloads but open to Dedicated for lower friction if KMS and network isolation guarantees met. Agreed next steps: send attestations, network architecture doc, schedule private-deploy deep-dive.
topics: RBAC and least privilege for API & console

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-14
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Thompson (CISO, Catalyst), Aisha Patel (Head of Eng), Tom Reyes (DevOps), Lina Gomez (Security Architect)

Summary (auto): Security posture discovery for potential Redwood deployment. Customer leans private for PHI, wants clear answers on KMS, audit logs, SSO, and retention.

00:00 Jordan Hayes: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, i'm Jordan from Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer. appreciate you taking the time.
00:07 Mark Thompson: thanks Jordan, yeah quick intro - i'm Mark, CISO at Catalyst. couple of key guardrails up front: we handle patient data, so we need SOC2 attestation, iso27001, and we have strict encryption and retention policies.
00:18 Jordan Hayes: totally understood, that's what we want to dive into. rough agenda - go over compliance artifacts, auth and identity flows, encryption/KMS, audit logs, and then discuss hosting options (hosted api, dedicated, private).
00:30 Aisha Patel: quick hi from my side, i'm aisha, head of engineering, mostly here for architecture and network questions.
:--
02:05 Priya Nair: to start on compliance - we're SOC2 Type II and have ISO27001 certificate, we can share the report and scope. our SOC2 covers our control plane and data handling for hosted environment; for Dedicated we provide contract language and for Private deployments you control the data plane entirely.
02:22 Tom Reyes: when you say "control plane" - what logs and data remain with Redwood in hosted mode? specifically anything that could include PHI?
02:35 Priya Nair: good question - by default hosted API does not store raw customer data beyond short-term logs needed for debugging and billing. we have configurable data retention windows; for PHI workloads we typically recommend Dedicated or Private. note: some transcription might say redwood private cloud but we mean our Private option with customer VPC.
03:00 Mark Thompson: so for Hosted, is there an option for customer-managed keys? we need CMEK for any data at rest that could be considered PHI.
03:12 Jordan Hayes: hosted currently supports service-managed encryption; for customer-managed keys we support Dedicated and Private. Dedicated can be set up with KMS integration depending on cloud provider; Private supports on-prem HSM/CMK.
03:25 Lina Gomez: and rotation? does Redwood rotate keys or do we have full control?
03:30 Priya Nair: for Private you have full control; for Dedicated we can work with your KMS so you control rotation policies. for hosted we rotate keys on our side and provide key lifecycle docs but cannot use a customer KMS for hosted API.
03:48 Aisha Patel: ok that aligns with what we expected.

05:15 Jordan Hayes: let's talk identity - SSO, SAML, SCIM - what do you need?
05:20 Mark Thompson: SAML for console access, SCIM for provisioning and deprovisioning, and we need assertion attributes to map to RBAC roles. also we want to make sure we can audit who called which model and when.
05:33 Priya Nair: Redwood supports SAML SSO for Console, SCIM for user sync, and OIDC for service auth. We can map SAML attributes to roles - Admin, Developer, Auditor. API keys can be scoped and rotated. Audit logs capture API calls, model used, request metadata, and user id when available.
06:02 Tom Reyes: format and retention for those audit logs? we need to ship to our SIEM (splunk) and keep logs for 7 years for certain events.
06:12 Priya Nair: logs can be exported via streaming to your S3 or to our webhook/syslog or forwarded to SIEM via partner connectors. retention defaults are configurable; hosted has limits on retention unless you add log retention add-on - Dedicated and Private give you full control over retention. we'll include log schema in the artifacts.
06:35 Mark Thompson: 7 years is a long time - are there storage implications or extra costs?
06:40 Jordan Hayes: yes, extended retention is an add-on; we'll include pricing options in the follow-up. Dedicated vs Private differences affect egress costs too.

09:05 Aisha Patel: on RBAC we need fine-grained controls: who can create deployments, who can call production models, who can view logs, and the ability to require mfa for admin roles.
09:18 Priya Nair: we have role-based controls with customizable roles; admins can create buckets/keys and set policies. MFA enforced via your identity provider for SSO. For API keys we support short-lived tokens via OIDC to reduce standing keys.
09:35 Lina Gomez: can we restrict export of model outputs? some of our use cases generate PHI and we want the outputs to never leave our VPC in certain flows.
09:45 Priya Nair: in Private deployment that's straightforward - data never leaves customer network. In Dedicated we can enforce network isolation and private peering; we also have data handling policies that can block certain exports but need to scope via a policy. For hosted, it's tougher - hosted managed environment isn't suitable for strict PHI blocking.
10:12 Mark Thompson: sounds like Private is likely then. but we need to understand the operational burden. what's the install footprint and support model?
10:25 Jordan Hayes: Private is a customer-controlled deploy - you run inference nodes in your VPC or on-prem. Redwood provides control plane (optionally in customer-managed or Redwood-managed mode) and orchestration. We have an on-prem bundle and a VPC package; typically network team will need to open certain ports and we provide a guided runbook. Support/SLAs are part of enterprise package.

12:05 Tom Reyes: what about software provenance and pen test results? we need SBOM, third-party vuln scans, and pen test reports.
12:15 Priya Nair: we can provide SBOMs for our binaries, dependency lists, and recent pen test summaries. full pen test reports are available under NDA.
12:27 Mark Thompson: and certifications - ISO, SOC2 - what's in-scope?
12:32 Jordan Hayes: our SOC2 Type II covers availability, security and confidentiality controls of the service. ISO27001 scope doc we'll share; it covers the platform and operational processes for hosted environment. For Dedicated and Private certain controls shift to customer responsibility.

15:00 Aisha Patel: on network connectivity - we need to know ports, subnets, NAT, and egress IPs for allowlist.
15:10 Priya Nair: we'll send a VPC runbook that lists required outbound ports for agent/control plane, IP ranges for allowlisting, and guidance for private peering. For Dedicated we can provide IP ranges, for Private we provide specifics during provisioning.

17:40 Tom Reyes: about data retention - we have retention policy of 6 years for patient records but for logs maybe 7 years. For model inputs/outputs we want to retain raw inputs for 90 days only, then purge. Is purging supported?
17:55 Priya Nair: yes, we support retention policies per dataset/route. For hosted we store minimal request logs; with Dedicated/Private you can configure automatic purge. We also support manual deletion via APIs. We'll note constraints where backups or snapshots might retain data - docs will call that out.

20:30 Lina Gomez: encryption at rest - do you offer AES-256, and for customer keys do you support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault? HSM tie-ins?
20:44 Priya Nair: yes AES-256 for at-rest. We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault integrations for Dedicated; Private can support HSMs and bring-your-own-key. Key rotation is supported and you can rotate with minimal downtime; we'll detail step-by-step and our recommended rotation cadence.
21:10 Mark Thompson: how do you handle ephemeral cache like KV cache - does it ever get persisted?
21:20 Priya Nair: KV caches are in-memory on the inference nodes; we don't persist them to long-term storage unless configured. For Private, since nodes run in your environment, you control node snapshots. For Hosted we periodically scrub caches and have memory-only policies but we'll include the technical note.

24:00 Jordan Hayes: any blockers from your legal/compliance perspective for us to proceed to pilot?
24:08 Mark Thompson: we need to review SOC2 and ISO docs, get a network deep-dive with Tom and Lina, and confirm KMS/HSM support. Also would like to confirm log export format (json lines) and SIEM compatibility.
24:22 Jordan Hayes: great - we'll send those artifacts. Priya will follow up on the VPC runbook and log schema.

26:15 Tom Reyes: what about model governance - can we restrict which models are available to a tenant? we don't want experimental open weights being used in prod.
26:25 Priya Nair: yes, you can pin model catalog per tenant and restrict which model versions are allowed. For Dedicated/Private you can also bring your own model binaries. We also offer policy controls to prevent use of unapproved models in certain endpoints.

29:00 Aisha Patel: backups - if nodes are stateful for caching or other reasons how are snapshots handled and who controls snapshot storage?
29:10 Priya Nair: snapshots are stored in customer-owned storage for Private and can be encrypted with customer KMS. For Dedicated we offer options. For hosted we manage snapshots per our retention policies and can provide delete/retention APIs.

32:40 Mark Thompson: audit logs - we need immutable audit trails for admin actions and data access events. Ideally those are write-once and forwarded to our SIEM.
32:50 Priya Nair: we support append-only audit logs and can forward to your S3 or SIEM in real time. For additional immutability we support write-once buckets and signing. We'll include example queries for common compliance checks.

35:05 Jordan Hayes: on the legal side - we've got standard DPA and BAAs (business associate agreements) for PHI - do you need a BAA?
35:15 Mark Thompson: yes we will need a BAA for PHI handling.
35:22 Jordan Hayes: we have a standard BAA for enterprise plans; legal can start a redline after we share SOC2 scope and technical docs.

38:00 Lina Gomez: any latency/security tradeoffs with encryption in transit vs at rest? e.g., TLS, mutual TLS for internal services?
38:10 Priya Nair: we use TLS everywhere for in-transit. Private deployments can enable mTLS between control plane and inference nodes if you prefer; that adds an operational step but it's supported. Latency impact is minimal.

41:20 Tom Reyes: are there any known limitations for on-prem GPUs, like driver versions or kernel compat? we run on a mix of NVIDIA ampere and older runtimes.
41:32 Priya Nair: we publish supported hardware matrix; older GPUs might need specific kernels and we can provide a compatibility shim for certain inference stacks. We'll run a compatibility check during onboarding.

44:00 Jordan Hayes: recap - deliverables: SOC2/ISO docs, VPC runbook, log schema, pricing for Dedicated vs Private, schedule network deep-dive for 2026-03-20. action owners noted.
44:12 Mark Thompson: sounds good. thanks Jordan and Priya.
44:18 Jordan Hayes: thanks all - we'll follow up via email with artifacts.
44:22 Aisha Patel: thanks, bye.

(End of recording)
notes: Call had typical transcription noise: some product names slightly mis-transcribed (e.g., Redwood Private Cloud -> Redwood private), timestamps approximate. Customer preference: Private for PHI, with Dedicated as secondary if KMS and network isolation satisfy requirements.
